subject: SIG evidence request: failover & RTO/RPO artifacts — SignalMesh
messages:
From: Kate Willis <kate@signalmesh.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: security@signalmesh.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG pre-review: RTO/RPO evidence needed for SignalMesh integration

Hi Jordan,

SignalMesh is scheduling our SIG-assessment of the integration with Redwood next week. As part of the pre-review packet we need artifacts demonstrating recovery behavior for the inference surface — specifically:

- documented runbook for a regional failover (play-by-play)
- time-stamped KV/no-KV warmstart snapshots and logs for recent warm failovers
- RTO and RPO measurements from last two drills and the method used to measure them
- any automated failover test traces or video capture (if available)

Target deadlines: we need the packet uploaded by 2026-11-18 to include it in the SIG folder. If some pieces are sensitive, we can accept an encrypted link or a controlled Drive folder with viewer-only access for the reviewers.

Quick answers that reviewers will look for: what is your typical cold-start RTO for a 2xGPU shard, warmstart RTO with KV cache, and RPO during a cross-AZ failover?

Can you confirm ownership and a point of contact who can walk the reviewers through the artifacts on 2026-11-19 (30 minute walkthrough preferred)?

Thanks,
Kate Willis
Security Lead
SignalMesh

Attachments: none in this message
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kate Willis <kate@signalmesh.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG pre-review: RTO/RPO evidence needed for SignalMesh integration

Kate — thanks for the heads up.

We can assemble the packet. Triage notes below and next steps:

- Ownership: Priyom (Platform Reliability) will own the artifacts and handoff.
- Short answers up front: typical warmstart RTO w/ KV cache: ~45s (median), cold-start RTO for a 2xGPU shard: ~6–8 min depending on model checkpoint size, RPO for automated failover with prefix/KV caching: ~<1 min (most traffic continues with KV replay); cross-AZ failover RPO depends on replication config but our standard profile for hosted customers is 1–5 min. We will provide exact drill timestamps and measurement scripts.

Action items:
1) Priyom — collect runbook, latest warmstart logs and the KV snapshot tarball, and a concise measurement methodology (how we measured RTO/RPO).
2) Ben — please add cost/throughput notes for the 2xGPU shard example (helps reviewers reason about timelines).
3) Rishi — provide the security redaction checklist for artifacts we place in shared Drive.

Timeline: Priyom, can you upload a zipped packet to the Drive link below by EOD 2026-11-17? If anything is sensitive, flag it and we’ll provide an encrypted DocuSign / secure share. I can do the 30-minute walk-through on 2026-11-19 at 10:00 PT if that works for SignalMesh.

Drive upload location (placeholder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_drive_link

Jordan Blake
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Kate — attaching the packet for initial review. Notes below.

What’s attached (zipped packet uploaded to Drive and attached here as stubs):
- redwood_runbook_v3.pdf — production failover runbook (step-by-step, contact tree, decision points).
- kv_cache_snapshot-20261114.tar.gz — KV snapshot used in the Nov 14 warmstart (contains metadata only; keys redacted in the public zip).
- warmstart-log-20261115.txt — concatenated warmstart traces collected during our last tabletop drill.

Summary & method:
- Drill dates: 2026-09-21 (tabletop), 2026-11-14 (live warmstart), 2026-11-15 (follow-up verification).
- Measurement method: we instrumented the client-facing routing layer to emit a T=0 marker at failover trigger and marked the first successful response for a canonical 512-token generation. All timings in warmstart runs are captured in warmstart-log-20261115.txt with epoch timestamps and request ids.
- Observed numbers (median over 50 runs during the Nov 14 warmstart): warmstart RTO (KV present): 42s median, 95th percentile 78s. Cold-start RTO (no KV, model reload): median 7m 5s, 95th percentile 9m 20s. RPO: KV replay lost <1 minute of in-flight requests in all tested scenarios; for cold failovers we saw up to 4 minutes of state lag in a degenerate replication config.

Redaction & sensitive data: KV payloads are redacted; keys are replaced with stable hashes to preserve timeline analysis without exposing customer content. Rishi — please confirm the redaction check before we mark the Drive folder as shareable.

Attachments (stubs): redwood_runbook_v3.pdf (PDF), kv_cache_snapshot-20261114.tar.gz (archive), warmstart-log-20261115.txt (text)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_drive_link (packet: SIG_pre-review_SignalMesh.zip)

If SignalMesh wants a live 30-minute walkthrough, Jordan — I can join at 10:00 PT on 2026-11-19 and walk through the runbook and log traces.

Best,
Priyom Das
Platform Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priyom — packet received and preliminary review looks fine. A few quick follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm the exact measurement script we used (we want to reproduce the T=0 marker approach)? If you can attach the script or a short snippet that would be ideal.
2) For the warmstart logs, can you add a 1-line summary per log file (e.g., sample request-id + observed latency) to the top of warmstart-log-20261115.txt so our auditors can quickly scan?
3) Please upload the DocuSign access link for the confidentiality addendum (SignalMesh requires a signed NDA before reviewers access logs). We use a short DocuSign template — you can send it to security@signalmesh.com.

We’ll target the 30-minute walkthrough on 2026-11-19 at 10:00 PT — that works for the review panel. Please send the docusign link and the updated log summary by EOD 2026-11-18.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Kate

Kate Willis
